description: Analytic line clipping, source-index provenance, wave growth and source-bearing region merge contracts. Each probe must fail through an ordinary geometry assertion.

mutants.old: result.back().clipped = false; // Mark the end of the clipped line
mutants.new: result.back().clipped = true; // Mark the end of the clipped line
mutants.test_filter: Line splitting clips the path around expolygon holes
mutants.description: Keep the final junction of a clipped interval marked as clipped. The diagonal-through-hole oracle then incorrectly includes the interval across the hole and fails its expected clipped endpoints.

mutants.test_filter: Closed line splitting omits the duplicate endpoint
mutants.description: Invert the closed-path guard so the duplicated start junction remains. The closed rectangle fixture requires an open storage cycle with the duplicate removed and fails as an ordinary assertion.

mutants.test_filter: Line splitting keeps source indices for boundary-overlap runs
mutants.description: Break the negative-index encoding for generated intersection junctions. The boundary-overlap fixture requires the entry and exit junctions to map to source edges 0 and 4.

mutants.test_filter: Region merge selects the source-bearing component among detached expansion fragments
mutants.description: Select the first merged component instead of the one containing the original source sample. The detached expansion is deliberately left of the source-bearing merged component; bounds and area assertions detect the wrong selection.

mutants.test_filter: Wave expansion grows a closed seed and clips it to its boundary
mutants.description: Use one fewer subsequent offset wave when nsteps > 1; the case's public bounds must no longer reach the expected 10 mm expansion.

mutants.test_filter: Wave seeds retain source IDs across shared boundary vertices
mutants.description: Subtract the boundary sequence origin rather than the source sequence origin. The decoy source makes the target source ID nonzero, so the provenance CHECK must fail normally.
